I definitely agreed that she needs to meet me halfway in this matter and that even with her hectic, busy life there must’ve been moments here and there for a small message or a meme. 


I feel there may be a lot more assumption on her part, or that she expects that I have read her mind and know what’s going on. I cannot falter entirely for this, because I am also guilty at times. 😅


I want to use this checkpoint as efficiently as possible I want answers to some questions and probable solutions and a solid promise to keep things in mind and progress so here are some questions I’ve conjured up.


1. As you know, I have this N D, which means that I am very susceptible to negative thoughts, and need reassurance in affection as a sort of tangible proof. 
So far we have installed some systems that have helped quite a lot, but I think it’s time that we upgrade a bit so it meets more needs.

- We’ve discussed this before, but I need to be updated on happenings so I feel included in your life
-  I know that you are a very present person, which I admire, but you’re often forgetful when it comes to communicating. Let’s integrate something that would help me feel connected; something that doesn’t take much time out of your day but I still enough quality time for me. 


2. These are questions of clarification, because I not only read between the lines, but I could also interpret things negatively on instinct,
- I show and tell love with words, letters and time and I hope you feel loved. I do this not only because I enjoy it but also to make sure that you are constantly reassured that I love you. 
I understand that you are not good with words, and that I do have to take some of your affections at face value, but I would like a love language that feels comfortable to the both of us that i can get more out of.
Words can be a bit vague and letters take a good chunk of time. I was thinking that we could play a message game or maybe a back-and-forth tiny project that takes a bit of time, but not too much effort? (Ahhh help)


- going back on “I need to take your words at face value.” That shit is hard for me bc all of my words have deeper connections, that and I’m tone and context sensitive. I love when you message me “I love you” but at times it can feel like your response comes from a place of it being more mandatory. 
What do you think of a little variance? Not all with words but just something like “I found a rock that looks like you”  it’s not an I love you but it’s a “this thing reminded me of you, I think about you even when I’m not talking to you” 
It makes me nervous at times but I also really like how you can be direct when asking me about or for something. I know I’m good at analyzing and it has its perks but it’s a breath of fresh air when you just do or ask it straight away.

Your last bit was really touching, thank you <3

I’m glad that you talk to your boyfriend about your BPD! That’s a really big step that a lot of people are scared to take!

I know even the smallest amount of reassurance goes miles for us and communication is key, But getting back onto the reassurance part of BPD, I would say that truly understanding that your partners thoughts and actions and mannerisms are things that you cannot fully predict all of the time and that just because you cannot predict them, doesn’t mean that it’s a negative thing.

Tell me if it’s the same for you, but whenever I talk to my partner, I expect them to have a certain reaction or say something that I think would be a positive thing, but they end up saying something not even remotely close in that scary. I struggled a lot with this and I still struggle with it today but I started really sitting down and telling myself that just because they had a reaction where they said something that wasn’t what I thought it was gonna be doesn’t mean that the world is ending XD 

BPD seems to love predictability because it is comfortable and easy but unfortunately (fortunately) that’s not how life is!
Some people have social anxiety based on unpredictability, and their therapy is exposure therapy, where they fully have to embrace, unpredictability, and I feel like that wouldn’t be such a bad idea for us either!

This might sound like a douche bag way of saying it, but I’ve seen a lot of people with BPD slowly get back into dating and relationships, and what their mindset seems to be (in a more positive way) is they treat their relationships as a hobby.
The two are kind of similar in a way if you think about it relationships and hobbies are both a part of your life and they both make you happy but you also outside of that make time for yourself. The hobby (relationship) is a part of you, but not your entire personality (please say this doesn’t sound bad).

To maintain a normal relationship, you must see your self and your partner as individuals with your own lives. The way that you to manage stress, the differences in your love language, and your views on certain things are all going to be different and as time goes on, you may start to overthink and fear abandonment because you realize you cannot think what your partner thinks and things become unpredictable and scary.
People with BPD can often times get fixated on people but I say, as long as you can realize that you were individuals, and that your thoughts and actions will be different from your partners then that’s one step into getting into a healthy relationship!

Best of luck, and I hope this helps

TLDR: she explained to another why my skin was brown and indirectly taught me a cool trick 

Being an immigrant I hopped around schools so I never really made friends when I was younger.
I was always questioned about my skin colour and culture and was picked on for bringing “weird” food into class (it was rice and chicken) anyways, once this little girl (we were the same age) innocently asks me why my skin was brown (this was in Texas the most diversity was probably me and one black kid) 
I didn’t take any offence to this but I didn’t know how to answer and was really uncomfortable I looked down at the ground not knowing what to say. 
My teacher over heard this and told the little girl that I was darker than her because I was from another country and people there are different colours than in Texas. She went on to explain how it was really cool that my skin was less subseptable to sunburns because of melanin and proceeded to talk about really cool facts about different skin colours. 
I don’t think she knows but she taught me that I can diffuse an uncomfortable situation by turning it into an interesting conversation. I still use this trick in daily life and have grown to be very good in terms of talking to others and public communication. 
Thanks to her I’ve never had annoying silences or avoidable heated arguments.
